idiom_name: JPA/Hibernate @Inheritance strategies with a discriminator column
implementation_notes: The JPA provider generates the mapper hierarchy from the entity hierarchy: @Inheritance(strategy = SINGLE_TABLE|JOINED|TABLE_PER_CLASS) on the root entity selects the table strategy (SINGLE_TABLE is the default when the annotation is absent), @DiscriminatorColumn/@DiscriminatorValue carry the type code, and EntityManager.find returns the concrete subclass because the provider resolves the polymorphic identity. Hand-written mapper classes stay justified only where statements must be controlled individually - MyBatis resultMaps with a discriminating case, or JDBC row mappers - which is the alternative variant.
pitfalls: SINGLE_TABLE is the default: omitting @Inheritance silently maps the whole hierarchy into one table with nullable subclass columns.
TABLE_PER_CLASS polymorphic queries become UNION ALL over all concrete tables and are not required to be supported by every provider; use it for independent reads, not for base-class traversals.
Subclass associations touched after the transaction closes throw LazyInitializationException - a mapper that walks the hierarchy outside the session fails where a plain find worked.

variants.idiom_name: JPA/Hibernate @Inheritance strategies with a discriminator column

variants.name: MyBatis resultMaps with a discriminator element
variants.implementation_notes: MyBatis gives no mapper generation, so the mapper hierarchy is written: one resultMap per class, a base resultMap for the inherited columns, and a <discriminator> on the type column that selects the subclass resultMap per row (its nested cases are themselves resultMaps). That reproduces exactly the classic structure - abstract mapping in the base resultMap, concrete mapping in each case - while SQL stays hand-written.
variants.code_sketch:
<resultMap id="paymentResult" type="Payment">
  <id property="id" column="payment_id"/>
  <result property="name" column="name"/>
  <discriminator javaType="string" column="payment_type">
    <case value="card" resultMap="cardPaymentResult"/>
    <case value="transfer" resultMap="transferPaymentResult"/>
  </discriminator>
</resultMap>
<!-- cardPaymentResult extends="paymentResult" adds card_number -->
pitfalls: Result maps are built incrementally: a hand-written hierarchy that tries to be complete in one shot is where the wrong subclass gets instantiated.
The discriminator column must be selected explicitly in every query that uses the resultMap; a forgotten column silently yields the base type.
MyBatis resolves subtypes through the declared resultMap only - a class added to the domain but not to the discriminator has no representation at all.
